title: Push a seat belt shoulder anchor 45 mm up its pillar rail against the belt's pull, past two notches into the marked one
instruction: Raise the seat belt's shoulder anchor against the belt's pull to the top notch marked on the trim, so it locks there, and clear the hands.
context: Anyone who takes a car's front seat can set the shoulder belt anchor on the B-pillar, and a taller occupant raises it so the belt crosses the centre of the shoulder. The Toyota RAV4 owner's manual gives the act as "To raise: slide the anchor up" and adds "make sure the anchor is locked in position." The belt's retractor pulls the anchor down the whole way: stop between notches and it drops back to the last notch passed; press the release button and it falls to the bottom. The United States has 237,655,885 licensed drivers (FHWA Highway Statistics, table DL-22), and Toyota sold 475,193 RAV4s in the United States in 2024 (Toyota Motor North America, 2024 U.S. sales results), each with a height-adjustable shoulder belt anchor at both front seats. Americans make 2.1 trips a day on average (FHWA Mobility Trends briefs, 2022 National Household Travel Survey).
setup: A car's left B-pillar section stands beyond a cut-back table that carries the two arms (bases 61 cm apart), tilted 10 degrees from upright with its top towards the arms, the pillar's inward lean: a 3/4 in birch plywood board (18 mm, 30 x 59 cm, dark grey) in place of the pillar's sheet metal, on two 1-1/2 in aluminium round tube posts. Bolted to it through its rail's two end holes, as in the car: a Toyota RAV4 (2019 to 2025, XA50) front shoulder belt anchor adjuster, Toyota part 73200-12070 (about 75 USD). Over it, seated as in the car, the RAV4's upper centre pillar trim, Toyota 62420-0R060-B1 (light grey plastic, 3 mm, 11 cm wide flaring to 17 cm at its foot, 42 cm tall), with the adjuster's black slider (41 mm wide, 85 mm tall) in its 50 x 157 mm window; below it the lower pillar trim with the webbing's slot. The slider carries the anchor stud, collar and nut (dark metal) at its top and a raised block above the white lock release button (21 x 14 mm, 4 mm proud, sprung: 10 N pressed in full) at its lower edge. The D-ring of the front belt assembly, Toyota 73220-06390-C3 (60 mm wide, a 50 x 10 mm webbing slot), hangs from the stud, turned towards the seat; the belt's 48 mm black webbing runs from the lower trim's slot up through the D-ring and back down beside the seat. Forward of the pillar stand the outboard edge of the front seat's back and its headrest (dark grey), out of the hand's path. The stud is 1.16 m above the ground and 30 cm in front of the arm bases at the top notch. The rail has five notches 15 mm apart (60 mm of travel); the anchor starts locked at the second-lowest notch, 45 mm below the top notch, marked by yellow tape on the trim; the belt's retractor pulls the webbing taut. One overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Real-trial checks: after the hands clear, a light downward tug of about 5 N does not move the anchor; the video shows the anchor at the tape; a ruler or side photo gives the 10 mm and 3 mm marks.
scoring: 0.33: the anchor at least 10 mm above its start notch. 0.67: the anchor within 3 mm of the marked top notch. 1.0: the pawl caught in the marked notch, the release button out (within 1 mm of its rest), and both whole grippers (fingers, palm and housing) at least 2 cm from the anchor, held 3 s. The belt's pull acts on the anchor throughout: a locked anchor gives way upwards only to a push above the pull and the pawl's ramp, an anchor let go between notches drops back to the last notch passed, and a pressed button lets it fall to the bottom. Void (0): a locked anchor forced more than 3 mm below its notch (checked from 0.5 s after the pawl drops). Real trial: a ruler or side photo for the 10 mm and 3 mm marks; a light downward tug (about 5 N) on the anchor must not move it; the video must show it at the tape.
fidelity: Rigid, 240 Hz. Pillar, rail, trims fixed. Anchor 0.22 kg on a prismatic joint, 60 mm, friction 0.5 N, starts 45 mm down. Pawl is code: locked, a 50 kN/m spring that gives way at 9.8 N, down too (a real pawl holds down; 3 mm down voids) (6.8 N belt pull: retractor 3 N, FMVSS 209: 1 to 7 N, on both webbing legs plus weight; 3 N ramp, estimate) and clicks into a notch within 1.5 mm; button in 2 mm frees it to the pull. Webbing: rigid stand-in, no collider. Estimates bounded in README.
